title: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Rules
description: Rules governing integration with external systems (Jira, Trello, Linear, GitHub, Confluence). ACLs normalize and validate external data against Core artifacts, preventing external chaos from contaminating Evolith governance.

principles.statement: All external data ingested into a satellite product MUST be validated against Evolith Core schemas before entering the governance model. Unvalidated data MUST be rejected.
principles.rationale: Without schema validation, external systems can introduce non-compliant entities that violate Core definitions. ACL acts as the gatekeeper.
principles.validationQuery: ACL implementation validates incoming payloads against Core JSON schemas (evolith-yaml.schema.json, artifact schemas). Invalid payloads return error and are logged.

principles.statement: Every transformation applied to external data MUST preserve traceability to the original external source entity. Audit trail MUST be maintained.
principles.rationale: When data is normalized, the original source must remain traceable for debugging, compliance, and impact analysis. Transformations without traceability create invisible data mutations.
principles.validationQuery: ACL transformation logs record: externalSourceId, externalSystem, transformationType, transformedToEntityId, timestamp. Logs retained per data retention policy.

principles.statement: Non-compliant data MUST be rejected, not normalized or silently adapted. ACL implementations MUST NOT perform silent data transformation to make external data fit Core schemas.
principles.rationale: Silent normalization hides governance gaps and creates technical debt. Rejection forces upstream systems to fix data quality at the source.
principles.validationQuery: ACL rejects non-compliant payloads with explicit error message identifying: field, expected format, actual value, external system origin. Rejection events are counted in governance metrics.

principles.statement: ACL implementations MUST be versioned alongside Evolith Core evolution. When Core schemas change, all ACL implementations MUST update before or at the same release.
principles.rationale: Version drift between ACL and Core creates incompatibility where external data appears valid but fails governance rules. ACL and Core must evolve in lock-step.
principles.validationQuery: ACL implementation declares coreCompatibilityVersion in its metadata. Validator checks ACL version is compatible with Core pinned version in evolith.yaml.

principles.statement: Integration with external systems MUST use explicit contracts (API specs, webhook payloads, export schemas) documented and reviewed against Core definitions before implementation.
principles.rationale: Ad-hoc integrations without contracts create implicit dependencies that break silently when external systems change.
principles.validationQuery: ACL integration documentation includes: externalSystem, contractVersion, mappedCoreEntities, transformationMatrix. Contract reviewed by Architecture Board if touching multiple bounded contexts.

principles.statement: ACL implementations MUST be isolated from domain logic. ACL code lives in Infrastructure/Adapters layer, never in Domain entities or application services.
principles.rationale: Domain purity requires zero external system references. ACL is the translation layer that keeps the Domain clean.
principles.validationQuery: Code analysis shows no imports from Jira, Trello, Linear, or similar external SDKs in Domain layer. ACL implementations are in /adapters or /infrastructure folders only.

governance.complianceVerification: ACL rules verified by impact-analysis-synchronizer.mjs during pre-commit when ACL directory or external integration files change.
governance.exceptionProcess: Architecture Board exception required for any ACL that performs silent normalization (violates ACL-03). Exception documents business justification and data quality remediation plan.
metrics: acl.rejected.count — rejected payload count per external system
acl.transformed.count — successful transformations per entity type
acl.version.drift — Core vs ACL version delta
acl.integration.count — number of active external integrations
